rationale: The addressees are the people experiencing distress, not agents causing it in an object. The inherited transitive-looking bekümmern obscures this intransitive/experiencer meaning, supported by its own example and the full verse.

summary: The negative mətʔaṯrutu is I Infectum in the inherited entry. Its tʔ- shape and the Arabic V etymology do not by themselves make it a synchronic Turoyo Detransitive.
The experiencer is encoded by the 2pl ending; the objectionable designation supplies an implicit stimulus. No overt stimulus preposition or object coding can be inferred from this one clause.
The permitted ʔṯr lookup confirms a related II entry with Detransitive distress forms. Treat it as a boundary/cross-reference question rather than moving the exactly attested tʔṯr token.
How should loan tʔṯr I be related to ʔṯr II Detransitive? Check productive morphology and native judgments before consolidating the entries.
